newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian govt denies blocking Naples airport deal.
newsitem.headline: Italian govt denies blocking Naples airport deal.

text.p: Italian Transport Minister Claudio Burlando on Monday denied reports he was blocking a deal whereby British airports operator BAA Plc would buy a 65 percent stake in Naples airport.
However he said the government was changing the legal status of the management concession of Naples Capodichino airport, which would increase its value.
The city of Naples announced last week that after months of negotiations, it had agreed to sell BAA a majority stake in Gesac, the company which operates Capodichino airport.
It said the accord would be signed shortly, but did not disclose how much the deal was worth.

Two Italian companies, SEA and ADR, which operate the main airports at Milan and Rome respectively, were reported to be furious after they failed in last minute bid to persuade Naples authorities to agree to an alternative deal. British newspapers reported that the Italian government was seeking to freeze the BAA accord to give SEA and ADR another chance to buy for the Naples hub, but Burlando said his ministry was only introducing new administrative guidelines.

"This means that Naples airport will have, like in Milan and Rome, total rather than provisional management rights. This, for example, will change the value of Capodichino but not the possibility of privatising it," he told a news conference.
"We aren't putting the brakes on anyone," he added. He did not say when the changes would be introduced.
Under the terms of the agreement reached last week, Capodichino would have been modernised and the runway extended.
"If anyone presents problems over the eventual sale, then this will be investigated by the Italian or European courts," Burlando said.
